summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, and chronic venous thromboembolism was admitted for progressive shortness of breath and an 80-pound weight gain over several months. She was diagnosed with acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, likely due to fluid overload, despite a low BNP, which can be falsely low in obesity. She responded well to intravenous furosemide and was transitioned to oral furosemide 60 mg twice daily. A right heart catheterization showed normal pressures, likely due to prior diuresis, supporting heart failure as the primary cause. She was also treated for an asymptomatic Enterococcus urinary tract infection with a five-day course of ampicillin. Obstructive sleep apnea was addressed with BiPAP initiation, which improved her sleep quality. Her supratherapeutic INR on admission led to temporary holding of warfarin and bridging with heparin during the catheterization; she was discharged on warfarin 10 mg daily with INR of 2.1. Her polymyositis was stable without flare, and anemia was noted as stable with iron studies ordered for outpatient follow-up. She was discharged home with instructions to monitor daily weights, continue BiPAP, and follow up with cardiology, pulmonary, rheumatology, and primary care.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
